title: Netflix Replaces Content Chief Bela Bajaria With Former Disney Executive Peter Rice
excerpt: Bajaria leaves after nearly a decade overseeing Bridgerton, Squid Game and Netflix's live-events push, as the streamer cuts about 1,000 jobs and faces slowing engagement growth.
body:
• Netflix has appointed former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice as chief content officer, effective 26 October, replacing Bela Bajaria.
  • Bajaria, who joined Netflix in 2016 and became content chief in January 2023, is leaving after nearly a decade overseeing hits including Bridgerton, Squid Game and Wednesday.
  • The change was announced a day after Netflix cut about 1,000 jobs, roughly 6% of staff, its largest layoffs since 2022.
  • For Indian and diaspora viewers, the handover matters because Bajaria championed international and local-language programming that expanded Netflix's non-English slate.

Netflix said on Thursday it has appointed Peter Rice as chief content officer, succeeding Bela Bajaria, who is leaving after nearly a decade at the company, according to Reuters. Rice will oversee content strategy from 26 October, covering series, films and live events across regions.

A decade that reshaped Netflix's slate

Bajaria joined Netflix in 2016 to build its unscripted programming, took charge of global television in 2020 and was named chief content officer in January 2023. Under her leadership the service released defining hits including Bridgerton, Squid Game and Wednesday, and pushed into live programming through multi-year deals with WWE and the NFL. Industry reports put the content budget she oversaw at roughly $20 billion.

Co-chief executive Ted Sarandos thanked Bajaria for a decade of leadership and for broadening the service's offering, according to The Hollywood Reporter India. Her rise — from an executive brought in to run unscripted television to one of the most powerful figures in global entertainment — made her one of the most prominent Indian-origin leaders in Hollywood.

"Netflix has fundamentally changed the way stories are made, shared and experienced around the world."

— Peter Rice, incoming Netflix chief content officer

Why Netflix is making the change now

The appointment arrives under pressure. Netflix announced the move a day after telling staff it would cut about 6% of its workforce, roughly 1,000 employees, in its biggest round of layoffs since 2022. The company faces doubts about sustaining growth as viewing time fragments across free, creator-led platforms such as YouTube and TikTok, and its shares have fallen sharply over the past year.

Rice brings a traditional television and film pedigree rather than a streaming background. He previously served as chairman of Walt Disney Television and chairman of general entertainment at Disney, and before that held senior roles at Fox, including running Fox Searchlight. Sarandos described him as an experienced operator at scale, and Rice has also been involved in planning content and ceremonies for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

What it means for viewers and the diaspora

Bajaria's tenure is closely associated with Netflix's international turn: local-language originals and non-English hits became central to growth, opening doors for Indian creators and stories aimed at global audiences, including viewers in the diaspora. Whether Rice maintains that emphasis will shape what Indian and South Asian programming gets commissioned in the next cycle.

What to watch

Rice starts on 26 October. Netflix reports third-quarter earnings on 20 October, when investors will get their first chance to question the reshuffle, the layoffs and the company's engagement outlook directly.
